- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -1.00) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip by 5–10% relative to prior low.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or align with 30-day moving average.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (e.g., 0.00 or 0.33), model overestimates mean reversion; adjust downward by 2–5% for 3–5 day horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., 1.00), model tends to over-forecast upward; apply downward bias of 3–7% for 10+ day horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture long-term mean reversion; apply a 10–15% downward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or negative over last 5–7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often lags; adjust forecast downward 1–3% for 1–3 days after sentiment reversal.
